brief: A free 3D globe for learning geography, on phones and desktops. Bhoo means Earth and gol means round; together they make the everyday Hindi word for geography. It should feel curious, calm and playful, like a well-made desk globe, and never childish.
criteria: Success: unlike grid globes and map pins, recognisable at 16 px, works in one colour on navy and on white, and pairs with a Devanagari wordmark.

concepts.name: Pale Blue Dot
concepts.idea: One small blue dot caught in a beam of sunlight, the way Voyager saw the Earth.
rationale: Carries the Carl Sagan story you were drawn to, with no globe cliché
The app can open the same way: a dot in a sunbeam that grows into the globe
A strong app icon; the favicon has its own drawing with a larger dot
The beam's 15° angle is repeated in the cut tops of the b, h and l, and a matching custom-drawn भूगोल completes the bilingual lockup

concepts.name: Patchwork
concepts.idea: The globe as four pastel countries, borders meeting like a political map.
rationale: Closest to the app itself: the same pastel political palette
Warm and toy-like, true to the desk-globe feel
Weaker on white backgrounds, and a globe is the category's expected sign

concepts.name: Tilt
concepts.idea: A plain disc on the Earth's real 23.5° axis, showing only at the poles.
rationale: The simplest mark, built on a true geography fact
Risk: can read as a balloon or a cartoon bomb

recommendation: Pale Blue Dot. It is the most ownable of the three, it tells the Sagan story in one image, it makes the strongest app icon, and it gives the app a ready-made opening animation.
next_steps: Pick a direction, or tell me what you like in each
Have a fluent reader check the custom भूगोल letterforms
Wire the icons and logo into the app, and run a trademark search
